description: Reduce the two-level shape-9 initial spectral-projector cost. brief-66 profiled shape 9 and found that after the CQR moves to 3xTF32, the largest remaining FP64 (d884gemm) block is the initial projector construction _pp(_pp(G)) / _pm(_pm(G)) at ~16 percent of the shape -- the P=(A+/-I)/2 applications that build the +/- invariant-subspace ranges. Cut it: (a) reduce the double projector application to single where the raw +/- separation still holds, and/or (b) start the projector from fewer random columns (the subspace only needs rank kp, not n), shrinking the n-by-n projector GEMM to n-by-kp. Watch the raw pre-CQR +/- separation (FP64 gives ~3.6e-10) stays tight enough that the downstream CQR + gate hold 0 fallback. Two-level path only.

SINGLE projector application (Yp=_pp(G), Ym=_pm(G); was double _pp(_pp)/_pm(_pm)). Halves the projector A@X FP64 nn d884gemm (2 inst each -> 1 each, ~10.8ms -> ~5.4ms projector), CONFIRMED by nsys. BUT trips a fallback storm: shape 9 39449->83287us (2.1x SLOWER), geomean 29018->31301 (+7.9%). nsys shows cuSOLVER sytrd4_cta (9.3%) + epilogue appear = mass per-matrix fallback. Single P+/P- leaves the extracted basis ~30deg off the true eigenspace (the existing double-apply comment); the CQR + NS-rescue can't pull orth under the 6.10e-3 gate. Shape 6 (mixed512) also 107542->135125. Confirms brief caveat: raw separation needs the double n*n projector at this width. 39/39, stream absent.

SINGLE projector apply + oversample(p=16) + energy-ordered eig-truncation of the block Gram (keep top-rank eigvecs). NUMERICALLY SOUND: 39/39 validate, diagnostic nbad=0/640 over 5 clustered reseeds (orth ~0.4x, eigr ~0.04x gate) -- proves single-apply CAN hold IF truncation is ENERGY-ordered (plain single+CQR and single+QR-truncate both nbad~635/640: they retain the -space leakage; energy-ordering drops it). BUT SLOW: shape 9 39449->161616us (4.1x SLOWER), geomean 29018->32963 (+13.6%). Root cause: the truncation's batched torch.linalg.eigh on the (640,358,358) Gram = cuSOLVER syevd per-matrix on 358-dim blocks ~4x the whole parent. Need an energy-ordered orthonormalizer WITHOUT a full Gram-eigh. 39/39, stream absent.

COMPLEMENT projector for the LARGER eigenspace + one sharpening apply. Solve the SMALLER block directly (double apply), build the LARGER block as deflate-off-small-basis + ONE sharpening P+/P- apply, replacing that block's SECOND full n*n@n*k_large projector GEMM. nsys shape 9: projector nn d884gemm 10.78ms->8.59ms (-20%), NO sytrd/syevd (0 fallback storm). Shape 9 39449->38339us (-2.8%), geomean 29018->28978 (-0.14%, sub-noise). 39/39, clustered-test orth TIGHTER than parent (0.011-0.019 vs 0.15-0.35). Numerically parent-equivalent (diag 5 reseeds nbad=1/640 == parent's nbad=1). Pure complement w/o sharpen unreliable (eigr 60-180x some seeds -> would fallback-storm). FP64 kept, stream absent.

3 trials on the shape-9 two-level projector cost. KEEPER = t3 b0758f1a4 @ geomean ~28,955us (2 reads 28932/28978, both < parent 29018; sub-noise but consistent), shape 9 39449->38304us (-2.9%), 39/39, 0 fallback across 8 clustered reseeds, stream absent, FP64 kept.

FINDINGS on the brief's two levers:
- LEVER 1 (single vs double apply): REFUTED as net-win. Plain single-apply (t1) halves the projector nn d884gemm (nsys 10.78->5.4ms) but TRIPS A FALLBACK STORM (shape9 2.1x slower, eigr~150x gate, cuSOLVER sytrd reappears, ~635/640 fall back) -- the 5e-6 -space leakage from the 1e-5 within-cluster jitter breaks the block. The ONLY numerically-sound single-apply (t2: oversample+ENERGY-ORDERED eig-truncation) is nbad=0/640 across 5 reseeds AND 39/39, BUT its batched torch.linalg.eigh on the (640,358,358) Gram = cuSOLVER syevd on 358-dim blocks = ~150ms >> the ~5.4ms saved (shape9 4.1x slower). FP32-Gram-eig barely faster + trips ~64/640. The 2nd projector apply IS the cheapest -space-leakage suppressor; every substitute costs more than the apply it replaces.
- LEVER 2 (fewer columns): ALREADY AT FLOOR. The projector is ALREADY sized to exact rank -- _pp(G[:,:,:kp]) is n*n@n*kp and _pm(G[:,:,kp:]) is n*n@n*(n-kp), NOT n*n@n*n. kp=342/km=170; the +space is kp-dim so no sampling below rank and no oversample to remove.

WIN (t3): COMPLEMENT projector for the LARGER eigenspace + one sharpening apply. Since P-=I-P+, only ONE block needs the full double apply -- solve the SMALLER block directly (double), build the LARGER as deflate-off-the-small-basis + ONE sharpening apply. nsys: projector nn d884gemm 10.78->8.59ms (-20%), 0 fallback. Numerically parent-equivalent-or-better (8-seed reseed 0/640, orth margins 0.009-0.19x, tighter than parent). Shape 6/11 provably unaffected (only shape 9 runs the projector path -- mixed routes whole-batch cuSOLVER, lapdense->sign_dc).

OPEN DIRECTIONS (manager to weigh): (1) shape 9 is only ~5% of geomean log-weight, so even a perfect projector halving is ~1% geomean -- this lever's ceiling is small. (2) Next-biggest shape-9 FP64 block is the CQR batch_trsm_right (15.2%, 5.58ms) + CQR Gram (~4.5ms) -- OFF this brief's projector scope but the real remaining shape-9 lever (brief-20 pinned FP64-CQR irreducible; worth a fresh brief testing a trsm-free block orthonormalizer given the complement now gives a well-conditioned +block). (3) The complement deflation still costs ~1.3ms; a cheaper deflation form or dropping the sharpen was unreliable (eigr 60-180x). (4) t3 pushes ~11% off the projector (measured), near the practical on-brief floor -- recommend combining t3's small clean shape-9 win into the global-best lineage since it is disjoint (touches only _eigh_twolevel, only shape 9 exercises it) and gate-safer than parent.
